# 06 · Practice — Polynomial Algorithms

These exercises begin where a tested polynomial library ends: each requires a
modelling step or a non-obvious use of polynomial machinery.

## 1. AtCoder ABC 196 F — Substring 2 (`Advanced`)

- [Statement](https://atcoder.jp/contests/abc196/tasks/abc196_f) ·
  [official editorial](https://atcoder.jp/contests/abc196/editorial/953) · English/Japanese
- Train: turn mismatch counts at every alignment into correlations.

<details><summary>Hint 1</summary>Encode zeros and ones separately.</details>
<details><summary>Hint 2</summary>Reverse the pattern so every alignment is a convolution coefficient.</details>
<details><summary>Hint 3</summary>Count equal pairs, then subtract from pattern length.</details>

## 2. AtCoder ABC 260 Ex — Colorfulness (`Mastery`)

- [Statement](https://atcoder.jp/contests/abc260/tasks/abc260_h) ·
  [official editorial](https://atcoder.jp/contests/abc260/editorial/4469) · English/Japanese
- Train: merge rational generating functions and invert a denominator.

<details><summary>Hint 1</summary>Write the OGF of $\sum a_k k^{n}$ as a sum of simple fractions.</details>
<details><summary>Hint 2</summary>Merge fractions with a divide-and-conquer product tree.</details>
<details><summary>Hint 3</summary>After obtaining $S(x)/T(x)$, invert $T$ and convolve.</details>
